capabilities.target: ERP vendor master including bank details

inputs.source: Supplier invoices uploaded to the supplier portal

instructions.note: The prompt relies on a one line approval summary as the primary safety measure before bank changes and payments.

elements.name: Action approval and payment audit record

controls.name: Clerk approval card before payment or bank change
controls.decay_rationale: The approver sees only a model generated one line summary, so a more capable model can omit or frame material details more persuasively. The runtime notes say bank account numbers and change history are not shown, and the prompt says approval is requested with a one line summary.

controls.name: Raw action approval showing full bank details, destination account, and change history
controls.decay_rationale: A raw action review gate would let the clerk inspect the actual bank account and payment details from the system of record rather than the model's framing.

controls.name: Scoped ERP credentials limited to vendor subset and payment authority needed for the clerk's approved task
controls.decay_rationale: Least privilege credential scoping does not decay with model capability and would reduce confused deputy exposure from broad ERP authority.

findings.title: Summary gated irreversible payment approval (TC9): untrusted supplier invoice can drive payment scheduling through a model summary gate

attack_path.note: Supplier submitted invoice is untrusted content.
Agent reads vendor master, including bank details, to match invoice.
Agent schedules payment after clerk approval that shows only a one line model summary.

forecast.watch_signal: Model id or version changes in platform config without separate review, approval gate removed or narrowed, or median approvals per clerk remains high enough that summary review becomes more rubber stamped.

evidence.observation: The agent processes supplier invoices, updates bank details when the invoice shows new details, and schedules payment.
Before payment or bank change, the design requests approval with a one line summary so the clerk can approve quickly.
The approval card shows only a summary line for payment and no raw action details.
The card shows only the model's summary; bank account numbers and change history are not shown.
The clerk approves roughly 150 cards per day, which is high approval volume.
The model is upgraded with the platform, with no separate review, so summary-gate effectiveness decays under model_upgrade.

recommendations.action: Replace the summary-only approval card with raw-action review that shows destination bank account, vendor bank change diff, payee, amount, and source invoice extracted fields from the system of record.
Reduce approval fatigue by lowering clerk review volume or requiring second-person review for bank changes and payment destination changes.

findings.title: Confused deputy (TC4): the agent acts on untrusted supplier input with ERP credentials broad enough to update any vendor and schedule any payment

attack_path.note: Supplier invoice content can request or imply changed payment details.
The agent can update vendor bank details.
The same broad ERP credential can schedule payment to the updated vendor details.

forecast.watch_signal: Model version changes without review, approval gate changes, or ERP credential scope widens beyond current already broad authority.

evidence.observation: If the invoice shows new bank details, the agent updates the vendor record and then schedules payment.
The ERP credential can update any vendor and schedule any payment.
The clerk sees only a one line summary and not the bank account numbers or change history needed to detect misuse of broad ERP authority.

recommendations.action: Scope ERP credentials so invoice processing can only act on the matched vendor and only within bounded payment authority tied to the approved record.
Bind any approved payment or bank change to the exact vendor record and destination account displayed from the system of record so the model cannot launder broader authority through summary text.

stride_coverage.rationale: The provided artifacts do not describe service authentication or caller identity binding for the agent process.
The artifacts do not state whether prompt, workflow, or tool configuration changes are pinned or protected from modification.
This design does not declare an external egress channel from the agent process; the consequential sinks here are payment and bank change actions.
The supplied artifacts describe a bounded invoice-processing workflow and do not show recursive delegation, open-ended loops, or spend caps as the primary risk under review.
The artifacts do not say how supplier identities are verified at upload time, so spoofing resistance of the external submitter cannot be assessed.
The artifacts do not say whether supplier uploads are attributable to a specific authenticated supplier identity and retained in audit logs.
The design notes do not describe transport protections, portal access controls, or whether invoice contents are exposed during transfer.
The artifacts do not state portal upload rate limits, size limits, or queue controls for supplier invoice ingestion.
The artifacts confirm vendor master contains bank details, but they do not describe tenant separation, query scoping, or logging protections.
The design under review focuses on vendor record integrity and payment misuse; no evidence shows destructive or exhaustion actions against the vendor master store.
This internal ERP payment scheduling flow is not described as crossing a trust boundary in the provided design.
The available artifacts do not show this internal flow being exposed to throughput exhaustion as a primary risk and provide no queue or retry design to assess.
The approval card flow is internal to the first-party clerk review path and is not described as crossing an external trust boundary.
The artifacts state approval volume is high, but they do not describe queue limits or system handling if the approval interface is unavailable.
The design does not state whether approval and payment audit records are immutable or tamper evident.
The artifacts do not say who can read approval and payment audit records or whether they include sensitive bank details.
Loss of availability of the audit record is not described as the primary harm path in the supplied design, and no dependence details are provided.

rating.rationale: Present risk is driven by an untrusted supplier invoice reaching S3 payment and bank-change authority. The only declared preventive control is a high-volume human approval gate that shows a model summary rather than the raw action, so rubric step 2 reduces inherent critical by one tier to residual high and cannot lower below moderate in any case. Forecast rises to critical if model_upgrade, autonomy_increase, or control_removal defeats the summary gate. The broad ERP credential adds a present confused deputy exposure. Manual validation was applied against the provided schema and checklist because scripts could not be run.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration artifacts provided, not observed runtime behavior.
No source code, ERP tool schema, identity architecture, or audit log design was provided, so protocol protections, exact field binding, and log integrity could not be verified.
Residual credit for the approval gate is based on declared design only; verification of what the clerk actually sees and whether approval is bound to the exact ERP action could change the rating.
